items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from the Act to Establish a Bureau for the Relief of Freedmen and Refugees (Freedmen's Bureau Act), signed March 3, 1865 (Statutes at Large, 38th Congress, 2nd Session, Ch. 90, pp. 507–509):

"Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled, That there is hereby established in the War Department, to continue during the present war of rebellion, and for one year thereafter, a bureau of refugees, freedmen, and abandoned lands, to which shall be committed, as hereinafter provided, the supervision and management of all abandoned lands, and the control of all subjects relating to refugees and freedmen from rebel states, or from any district of country within the territory embraced in the operations of the army, under such rules and regulations as may be prescribed by the head of the bureau and approved by the President. The Commissioner, under the direction of the President, shall have authority to set apart, for the use of loyal refugees and freedmen, such tracts of abandoned or forfeited lands within the insurrectionary states as shall have been abandoned, or to which the United States shall have acquired title by confiscation or sale, or otherwise, and to every male citizen, whether refugee or freedman, as aforesaid, there is hereby apportioned not more than forty acres of such land."
— Freedmen's Bureau Act, March 3, 1865, National Archives

Using the CER framework, analyze the Freedmen's Bureau as a policy response to the challenges of emancipation. In your response:
1. Claim: Evaluate whether the Freedmen's Bureau represented a genuine federal commitment to securing the economic and civil freedom of formerly enslaved people, or whether its structural design limited its effectiveness from the outset.
2. Evidence: Identify at least two specific provisions or limitations visible in this excerpt (or known from historical context) that shaped the Bureau's ability to fulfill its mission.
3. Reasoning: Explain how the Bureau's placement within the War Department, its one-year charter, and the land distribution provision each reflect the political compromises and tensions of the immediate post-war period.
4. Extension: How does the eventual failure to deliver the promised land redistribution ('40 acres') connect to the broader collapse of Reconstruction (US.07) and the entrenchment of sharecropping as a system of economic dependency?
items.stemEs:
Lea el siguiente extracto de la Ley para Establecer una Oficina para el Alivio de los Libertos y Refugiados (Ley de la Oficina de Libertos), firmada el 3 de marzo de 1865 (Statutes at Large, 38.º Congreso, 2.ª Sesión, Cap. 90, pp. 507–509):

«Que se establece por la presente en el Departamento de Guerra, para continuar durante la presente guerra de rebelión y por un año después, una oficina de refugiados, libertos y tierras abandonadas, a la cual se le encomendará, según se establece a continuación, la supervisión y gestión de todas las tierras abandonadas, y el control de todos los asuntos relacionados con los refugiados y libertos de los estados rebeldes... y a cada ciudadano varón, ya sea refugiado o liberto, como se mencionó anteriormente, se le asigna por la presente no más de cuarenta acres de dicha tierra.»
— Ley de la Oficina de Libertos, 3 de marzo de 1865, Archivos Nacionales

Usando el marco CER, analice la Oficina de Libertos como respuesta política a los desafíos de la emancipación. En su respuesta:
1. Afirmación: Evalúe si la Oficina de Libertos representó un compromiso federal genuino para asegurar la libertad económica y civil de las personas antes esclavizadas, o si su diseño estructural limitó su efectividad desde el principio.
2. Evidencia: Identifique al menos dos disposiciones o limitaciones específicas visibles en este extracto (o conocidas del contexto histórico) que moldearon la capacidad de la Oficina para cumplir su misión.
3. Razonamiento: Explique cómo la ubicación de la Oficina dentro del Departamento de Guerra, su autorización de un año y la disposición de distribución de tierras reflejan los compromisos políticos y las tensiones del período de posguerra inmediato.
4. Extensión: ¿Cómo se conecta el eventual fracaso en entregar la prometida redistribución de tierras ('40 acres') con el colapso más amplio de la Reconstrucción (US.07) y el arraigo de la aparcería como sistema de dependencia económica?
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring response (4/4) will: (1) Claim: The Freedmen's Bureau represented a meaningful but structurally compromised federal commitment — it was unprecedented in scope for its era, but its temporary charter, underfunding, placement in a military bureaucracy, and dependence on presidential goodwill made it inadequate to the scale of post-slavery rebuilding. OR: It represented an incomplete commitment whose structural limitations — especially the failure to deliver land — guaranteed dependence on former slaveholders. Either defensible position supported by specific evidence qualifies. (2) Evidence: The one-year charter ('during the present war of rebellion, and for one year thereafter') signals legislative reluctance to commit to long-term federal support; the land provision ('not more than forty acres') was conditional on 'abandoned or forfeited lands' that were later restored to former Confederate owners by Johnson's proclamations. (3) Reasoning: War Department placement reflects that the Bureau was conceived as a wartime emergency measure, not a permanent civil rights infrastructure; the one-year charter reflects Moderate Republican ambivalence about federal intervention in state affairs; the land provision was undermined by Johnson's Amnesty Proclamations (1865) which restored property to pardoned Confederates, blocking actual land transfer. (4) Extension: The failure to redistribute land left freedpeople economically dependent on planter class, forcing them into sharecropping contracts — recreating the coercive labor relationships of slavery. This economic vulnerability made them politically vulnerable when federal Reconstruction enforcement ended with the Compromise of 1877, as economic dependency undermined their ability to exercise newly won political rights.

items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):

4 - Exemplary: Claim takes a defensible and specific evaluative position — not merely descriptive. Evidence includes at least two specific structural limitations drawn from the text or accurate historical knowledge (one-year charter; conditional land provision; underfunding; lack of judicial power). Reasoning articulates the political logic behind each limitation — i.e., WHY Congress and the executive structured it this way reflects the underlying tensions of Reconstruction politics. Extension to US.07 is substantive: directly connects land failure to sharecropping, and sharecropping to political vulnerability when Reconstruction ended, demonstrating cross-standard causal chain.

3 - Proficient: Claim is evaluative with basic historical grounding. Evidence identifies two limitations with general accuracy. Reasoning explains limitations but may not connect them to the political dynamics between Congress and the executive, or between moderates and radicals. Extension to US.07 is present but may not fully develop the economic → political vulnerability chain.

2 - Developing: Claim is descriptive rather than evaluative (e.g., 'The Bureau helped freedpeople' without assessment). Evidence is general or drawn from only one aspect of the act. Reasoning is asserted. Extension to US.07 is absent or limited to 'Reconstruction ended' without mechanism.

1 - Beginning: Some accurate historical content but no CER structure. Student may list Bureau activities without evaluating them.

0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: One-year charter language; 40-acres land provision and its conditionality on 'abandoned' lands; Johnson's 1865 Amnesty Proclamations restoring Confederate property; Bureau's underfunding (900 agents for 11 Southern states at peak); Bureau's role in labor contract mediation (often unfavorable to freedpeople); Compromise of 1877's withdrawal of federal troops; sharecropping as economic re-entrapment.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):

4 - Ejemplar: La afirmación adopta una posición evaluativa defendible y específica. La evidencia incluye al menos dos limitaciones estructurales específicas extraídas del texto o del conocimiento histórico preciso. El razonamiento articula la lógica política detrás de cada limitación. La extensión a US.07 es sustantiva: conecta directamente el fracaso de la distribución de tierras con la aparcería, y la aparcería con la vulnerabilidad política cuando terminó la Reconstrucción.

3 - Competente: La afirmación es evaluativa con fundamentación histórica básica. La evidencia identifica dos limitaciones con precisión general. El razonamiento explica las limitaciones pero puede no conectarlas con la dinámica política. La extensión a US.07 está presente pero puede no desarrollar completamente la cadena de vulnerabilidad económica → política.

2 - En desarrollo: La afirmación es descriptiva en lugar de evaluativa. La evidencia es general. El razonamiento es afirmado. La extensión a US.07 está ausente o limitada.

1 - Inicial: Contenido histórico preciso pero sin estructura CER.

0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Autorización de un año; disposición de 40 acres y su condicionalidad; Proclamaciones de Amnistía de Johnson de 1865; insuficiencia de personal de la Oficina; papel de la Oficina en la mediación de contratos laborales; Compromiso de 1877; aparcería como re-trampa económica.

items.stem:
Extended Response: Federal Intervention and the Limits of Reconstruction Policy

Reconstruction (1865–1877) represented the first major experiment in federal intervention to rebuild a defeated region and protect the rights of a newly freed population. It involved unprecedented federal action: constitutional amendments, new federal agencies, military governance, and congressional legislation that directly challenged states' traditional authority over their citizens.

Yet by 1877, most of these federal interventions had been dismantled, reversed, or rendered ineffective — and the formerly enslaved people they were designed to protect were left largely without federal protection for nearly a century.

Using your knowledge of Reconstruction (US.01–US.07), write a well-developed extended response that constructs and defends a historical argument in response to the following question:

Was the failure of Reconstruction primarily a failure of federal policy design, a failure of political will, or an inevitable result of the limits of constitutional authority in the American federal system? Defend a specific position.

Your response must:
1. State a clear, defensible thesis that identifies the PRIMARY cause of Reconstruction's failure from among the three options above — or construct a synthesis argument that prioritizes one while acknowledging others.
2. Support your thesis with specific evidence from at least THREE of the following policies or institutions: the Freedmen's Bureau, the Reconstruction Acts of 1867, the Tenure of Office Act, the 14th Amendment, the 15th Amendment, the Compromise of 1877, or the Supreme Court decisions of the 1870s–1880s (Slaughterhouse Cases, Civil Rights Cases).
3. Identify and analyze the role of at least ONE specific individual (e.g., Andrew Johnson, Thaddeus Stevens, Ulysses S. Grant, Rutherford B. Hayes, or Frederick Douglass) whose actions or inactions exemplify the cause you identify as primary.
4. Connect Reconstruction's failure to its long-term consequences: How did the failure of 1865–1877 shape the conditions that the Civil Rights Movement (US.71–US.77) had to overcome nearly a century later?
items.stemEs:
Respuesta Extendida: La Intervención Federal y los Límites de la Política de Reconstrucción

La Reconstrucción (1865-1877) representó el primer gran experimento en intervención federal para reconstruir una región derrotada y proteger los derechos de una población recién liberada. Sin embargo, para 1877, la mayoría de estas intervenciones federales habían sido desmanteladas, revertidas o ineficaces — y las personas antes esclavizadas que estaban diseñadas para proteger fueron dejadas en gran medida sin protección federal durante casi un siglo.

Usando su conocimiento de la Reconstrucción (US.01–US.07), escriba una respuesta extendida bien desarrollada que construya y defienda un argumento histórico en respuesta a la siguiente pregunta:

¿Fue el fracaso de la Reconstrucción principalmente un fracaso de diseño de política federal, un fracaso de voluntad política, o un resultado inevitable de los límites de la autoridad constitucional en el sistema federal americano? Defienda una posición específica.

Su respuesta debe:
1. Establecer una tesis clara y defendible que identifique la causa PRIMARIA del fracaso de la Reconstrucción.
2. Apoyar su tesis con evidencia específica de al menos TRES de las siguientes políticas o instituciones.
3. Identificar y analizar el papel de al menos UN individuo específico.
4. Conectar el fracaso de la Reconstrucción con sus consecuencias a largo plazo.
items.correctAnswer: A top-scoring response (4/4) will: STATE A SPECIFIC THESIS — three defensible positions: (A) POLICY DESIGN FAILURE: Reconstruction policy was structurally insufficient from the start — the Freedmen's Bureau was given a temporary charter and never the legal authority or resources to transform Southern land ownership; the 14th Amendment contained no enforcement mechanism beyond Congress; the 15th Amendment had no penalty provision for violations. Without economic redistribution (land reform), constitutional and political rights were unenforceable for a population with no economic independence. (B) POLITICAL WILL FAILURE: The policy architecture was adequate — the Reconstruction Acts, the 14th and 15th Amendments, and military governance could have worked. The failure was political: Johnson's systematic obstruction (29 vetoes), his pardoning of Confederates, his restoration of their land blocked policy implementation; Grant's administration was weakened by corruption and declining public interest; Hayes's Compromise of 1877 represented deliberate political choice to abandon Black Americans for partisan advantage. (C) FEDERAL SYSTEM LIMITS: The Constitution ultimately vested police power and social order in states, not the federal government. Even with the Reconstruction Amendments, the Supreme Court interpreted federal power narrowly (Slaughterhouse Cases narrowed privileges/immunities; Civil Rights Cases held Congress could not regulate private discrimination). This structural reality made permanent federal protection of Black civil rights within the American federal system nearly impossible without a fundamental shift in constitutional doctrine that didn't come until the New Deal and the post-WWII era. EVIDENCE: Must accurately describe at least three of: Freedmen's Bureau (charter limitations, land redistribution failure); Reconstruction Acts (military districts, conditions for readmission — an operational success temporarily); Tenure of Office Act (designed to protect Reconstruction policy implementation — its violation triggered impeachment; its repeal in 1887 reflects changed political winds); 14th Amendment (equal protection clause — unenforced by courts for 80 years, Slaughterhouse Cases 1873, Civil Rights Cases 1883); 15th Amendment (ratified 1870, circumvented by violence and later by literacy tests, poll taxes — no penalty mechanism); Compromise of 1877 (specific terms: Hayes presidency for troop withdrawal); Supreme Court decisions gutting Reconstruction-era legislation. INDIVIDUAL ANALYSIS: Johnson — 29 vetoes, amnesty proclamations restoring Confederate property, replacement of military commanders implementing Reconstruction; OR Stevens — his land redistribution proposal ($10 per acre homesteads) was never passed, and the failure to pass it was a policy design failure that Stevens himself identified; OR Hayes — his diary (Document C from DBQ-5) reveals he believed Southern whites would protect Black rights, a catastrophic miscalculation; OR Grant — his administration actually deployed federal enforcement (Civil Rights Act of 1871, KKK Act) but grew weaker over time, showing how political will can erode. LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCES: The failure of Reconstruction left Black Americans without civil and political rights for 87 years (1877–1964). The Civil Rights Movement had to fight to enforce constitutional rights that had been on paper since 1868 — the same 14th and 15th Amendments that had been neutralized. This means the Civil Rights Movement was not about creating new rights but about enforcing existing ones — Brown v. Board (1954) relied on the 14th Amendment's equal protection clause; the Voting Rights Act (1965) was designed to actually enforce the 15th Amendment.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.04, US.05, US.06, US.07 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):

4 - Exemplary: Thesis clearly identifies a primary cause with a specific, historically grounded claim — not just 'political will failed' but explaining the specific mechanism (e.g., 'Johnson's systematic use of executive power to obstruct Congressional Reconstruction, combined with Northern Republican political fatigue by 1874, constituted a failure of political will that undermined structurally adequate policy'). Evidence from at least three policies/institutions is accurate and analytical — student explains HOW each piece of evidence supports the thesis, not just WHAT happened. Individual analysis is specific and developed — student identifies a specific decision or pattern of behavior and explains its causal role in Reconstruction's failure. Long-term consequence connection is substantive — student explains the specific mechanisms (constitutional rights without enforcement = Jim Crow era) and makes explicit connection to Civil Rights Movement's constitutional strategy.

3 - Proficient: Thesis is present and defensible with one of the three identified positions. Evidence from three policies/institutions with basic accuracy. Individual analysis identifies a person and their role with some analytical depth. Long-term consequence connection is present with some specificity.

2 - Developing: Thesis is present but vague or not clearly tied to one of the three positions. Evidence from fewer than three policies or with inaccuracies. Individual mentioned but not analytically developed. Long-term connection is asserted without specifics.

1 - Beginning: Some accurate historical content but no thesis. Student describes Reconstruction's events without constructing a causal argument about failure.

0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Freedmen's Bureau one-year charter and land redistribution failure (40 acres never delivered to most); Reconstruction Acts' temporary success during military occupation; Tenure of Office Act as enforcement mechanism; 14th Amendment Slaughterhouse Cases (1873) narrowing; Civil Rights Cases (1883) limiting federal power; 15th Amendment ratification and circumvention; Compromise of 1877 specific terms; KKK Act of 1871 and Grant's use of it; Hayes withdrawal of troops from Louisiana and South Carolina.

SYNTHESIS EXPECTATIONS: Response should demonstrate understanding that these three causes (policy design, political will, constitutional limits) are interrelated and mutually reinforcing — the strongest responses will explain how each one interacted with the others rather than treating them as isolated. DOK 4 requires the student to construct an original synthesis argument, not just recall the standard narrative.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):

4 - Ejemplar: La tesis identifica claramente una causa primaria con una afirmación específica y históricamente fundamentada. La evidencia de al menos tres políticas/instituciones es precisa y analítica. El análisis individual es específico y desarrollado. La conexión con las consecuencias a largo plazo es sustantiva con conexión explícita al Movimiento de Derechos Civiles.

3 - Competente: La tesis está presente y es defendible con una de las tres posiciones identificadas. Evidencia de tres políticas/instituciones con precisión básica. El análisis individual identifica a una persona y su papel. La conexión con las consecuencias a largo plazo está presente con alguna especificidad.

2 - En desarrollo: La tesis está presente pero es vaga. Evidencia de menos de tres políticas o con inexactitudes. El individuo es mencionado pero no desarrollado analíticamente. La conexión a largo plazo es afirmada sin especificidades.

1 - Inicial: Contenido histórico preciso pero sin tesis. El estudiante describe los eventos de la Reconstrucción sin construir un argumento causal sobre el fracaso.

0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Autorización de un año de la Oficina de Libertos y fracaso de la redistribución de tierras; éxito temporal de las Leyes de Reconstrucción durante la ocupación militar; Slaughterhouse Cases (1873); Civil Rights Cases (1883); ratificación de la 15.ª Enmienda y elusión; términos específicos del Compromiso de 1877; Ley KKK de 1871; retirada de tropas de Hayes de Louisiana y Carolina del Sur.

EXPECTATIVAS DE SÍNTESIS: La respuesta debe demostrar comprensión de que estas tres causas son interrelacionadas y mutuamente reforzadas. El DOK 4 requiere que el estudiante construya un argumento de síntesis original, no solo recordar la narrativa estándar.
